sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca viśeṣo 'sti mahāṃs tāta bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ tatrāgamaya bhadraṃ te bhūya eva puraṃdara
english: Bṛhaspati said: There is a great excellence in the high-souled Bhārgava, my son; go and acquire learning there once more, Purandara—blessings upon you.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ātmanas tu tataḥ śreyo bhārgavāt sumahāyaśāḥ jñānam āgamayat prītyā punaḥ sa paramadyutiḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Then that one of vast renown and surpassing splendor, seeking his own greater good, joyfully acquired knowledge anew from the Bhārgava.

sanskrit: tenāpi samanujñāto bhārgaveṇa mahātmanā śreyo 'stīti punar bhūyaḥ śukram āha śatakratuḥ
english: Granted leave even by him, the high-souled Bhārgava, the Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices said once again to Śukra, 'Is there yet a greater good?'

sanskrit: bhārgavas tv āha dharmajñaḥ prahrādasya mahātmanaḥ jñānam asti viśeṣeṇa tato hṛṣṭaś ca so 'bhavat
english: But the Bhārgava, knower of dharma, replied, 'The high-souled Prahrāda possesses knowledge of special excellence'; and thereupon Indra was delighted.

sanskrit: sa tato brāhmaṇo bhūtvā prahrādaṃ pākaśāsanaḥ sṛtvā provāca medhāvī śreya icchāmi veditum
english: Then the Chastiser of Pāka, having become a brāhmaṇa, that wise one approached Prahrāda and said, 'I wish to learn what is the highest good.'

sanskrit: prahrādas tv abravīd vipraṃ kṣaṇo nāsti dvijarṣabha trailokyarājye saktasya tato nopadiśāmi te
english: But Prahrāda said to the brāhmaṇa, 'I have no leisure, O bull among the twice-born, occupied as I am with the sovereignty of the three worlds; therefore I cannot instruct you.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇas tv abravīd vākyaṃ kasmin kāle kṣaṇo bhavet tatopadiṣṭam icchāmi yad yat kāryāntaraṃ bhavet
english: The brāhmaṇa then spoke these words: 'At what time will you have leisure? Whatever interval falls between your duties, then I wish to be instructed.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto 'bhavad rājā prahrādo brahmavādine tathety uktvā śubhe kāle jñānatattvaṃ dadau tadā
english: Then King Prahrāda was pleased with the expounder of the Veda, and saying 'So be it,' he imparted to him the truth of knowledge at an auspicious time.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo 'pi yathānyāyaṃ guruvṛttim anuttamām cakāra sarvabhāvena yadvat sa manasecchati
english: And the brāhmaṇa too, according to custom, rendered to his teacher unsurpassed service with his whole being, just as that one desired in his heart.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaś ca tena bahuśaḥ prāptaṃ katham ariṃdama trailokyarājyaṃ dharmajña kāraṇaṃ tad bravīhi me
english: And he was asked by the brāhmaṇa many times: 'How, O subduer of foes, did you obtain the sovereignty of the three worlds, O knower of dharma? Tell me the cause of it.'

sanskrit: prahrāda uvāca nāsūyāmi dvijaśreṣṭha rājāsmīti kadā cana kavyāni vadatāṃ tāta saṃyacchāmi vahāmi ca
english: Prahrāda said: I never bear ill will, O best of the twice-born, thinking 'I am king'; when the wise speak their wisdom, my son, I restrain myself and bear it patiently.

sanskrit: te visrabdhāḥ prabhāṣante saṃyacchanti ca māṃ sadā te mā kavyapade saktaṃ śuśrūṣum anasūyakam
english: Trusting in me, they speak freely and ever guide me; and when I am devoted to the path of wisdom, eager to listen and free of envy,

sanskrit: dharmātmānaṃ jitakrodhaṃ saṃyataṃ saṃyatendriyam samācinvanti śāstāraḥ kṣaudraṃ madhv iva makṣikāḥ
english: those teachers heap their instruction upon me—a man of righteous soul, conqueror of anger, self-controlled, with senses subdued—as bees gather honey from flowers.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ vāgagrapiṣṭānāṃ rasānām avalehitā svajātyān adhitiṣṭhāmi nakṣatrāṇīva candramāḥ
english: Thus, savoring the essences ground fine upon the tongue's tip of the learned, I stand above those of my own kind as the moon stands above the stars.

sanskrit: etat pṛthivyām amṛtam etac cakṣur anuttamam yad brāhmaṇamukhe kavyam etac chrutvā pravartate
english: This is the nectar upon the earth, this the unsurpassed eye: the wisdom on a brāhmaṇa's lips—having heard it, one goes forward in life.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca etāvac chreya ity āha prahrādo brahmavādinam śuśrūṣitas tena tadā daityendro vākyam abravīt
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'This is the highest good,' said Prahrāda to the expounder of the Veda; and then, having been served by him, the lord of the Daityas spoke these words.

sanskrit: yathāvad guruvṛttyā te prīto 'smi dvijasattama varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te pradātāsmi na saṃśayaḥ
english: I am pleased with your fitting service to your teacher, O most excellent of the twice-born. Choose a boon—blessings upon you—and I shall grant it, of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kṛtam ity eva daityendram uvāca sa ca vai dvijaḥ prahrādas tv abravīt prīto gṛhyatāṃ vara ity uta
english: 'It is already done,' said that brāhmaṇa to the lord of the Daityas; but Prahrāda, well pleased, said, 'Let the boon be taken nonetheless.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca yadi rājan prasannas tvaṃ mama cecchasi ced dhitam bhavataḥ śīlam icchāmi prāptum eṣa varo mama
english: The brāhmaṇa said: If you are gracious to me, O king, and if you wish my welfare, then I desire to obtain your conduct—this is my boon.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tataḥ prītaś ca daityendro bhayaṃ cāsyābhavan mahat vare pradiṣṭe vipreṇa nālpatejāyam ity uta
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Then the lord of the Daityas was both pleased and seized by great fear, for at the boon named by the brāhmaṇa he thought, 'This one is of no small power.'

sanskrit: evam astv iti taṃ prāha prahrādo vismitas tadā upākṛtya tu viprāya varaṃ duḥkhānvito 'bhavat
english: 'So be it,' Prahrāda said to him then, astonished; but having bestowed the boon upon the brāhmaṇa, he was filled with sorrow.

sanskrit: datte vare gate vipre cintāsīn mahatī tataḥ prahrādasya mahārāja niścayaṃ na ca jagmivān
english: When the boon had been given and the brāhmaṇa had departed, great anxiety came upon Prahrāda, O great king, and he could reach no certainty.

sanskrit: tasya cintayatas tāta chāyābhūtaṃ mahādyute tejo vigrahavat tāta śarīram ajahāt tadā
english: As he brooded thus, my son—O lord of great splendor—a radiance in bodily form, like a shadow given shape, then forsook his body.

sanskrit: tam apṛcchan mahākāyaṃ prahrādaḥ ko bhavān iti pratyāha nanu śīlo 'smi tyakto gacchāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Prahrāda asked that mighty-bodied being, 'Who are you?' It replied, 'Surely I am Conduct. Cast off by you, I now depart.'

sanskrit: tasmin dvijavare rājan vatsyāmy aham aninditam yo 'sau śiṣyatvam āgamya tvayi nityaṃ samāhitaḥ ity uktvāntarhitaṃ tad vai śakraṃ cānvaviśat prabho
english: 'In that excellent brāhmaṇa, O king, I shall dwell, O blameless one—he who, having become your pupil, was ever steadfastly devoted to you.' Having spoken thus, it vanished and entered into Śakra, my lord.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tejasi yāte tu tādṛgrūpas tato 'paraḥ śarīrān niḥsṛtas tasya ko bhavān iti cābravīt
english: When that radiance had gone, another of like form then issued forth from his body, and Prahrāda said, 'Who are you?'

sanskrit: dharmaṃ prahrāda māṃ viddhi yatrāsau dvijasattamaḥ tatra yāsyāmi daityendra yataḥ śīlaṃ tato hy aham
english: 'Know me, Prahrāda, to be Dharma. Where that most excellent of the twice-born has gone, there too I shall go, O lord of the Daityas; for where Conduct is, there am I.'

sanskrit: tato 'paro mahārāja prajvalann iva tejasā śarīrān niḥsṛtas tasya prahrādasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then another, O great king, blazing as it were with splendor, issued forth from the body of the high-souled Prahrāda.

sanskrit: ko bhavān iti pṛṣṭaś ca tam āha sa mahādyutiḥ satyam asmy asurendrāgrya yāsye 'haṃ dharmam anv iha
english: Asked 'Who are you?', that one of great splendor replied to him, 'I am Truth, O foremost lord of the Asuras; I shall follow Dharma hence.'

sanskrit: tasminn anugate dharmaṃ puruṣe puruṣo 'paraḥ niścakrāma tatas tasmāt pṛṣṭaś cāha mahātmanā vṛttaṃ prahrāda māṃ viddhi yataḥ satyaṃ tato hy aham
english: When that being had followed after Dharma, yet another being came forth from him; and questioned by the high-souled one, it said, 'Know me, Prahrāda, to be Right Practice; for where Truth is, there am I.'

sanskrit: tasmin gate mahāśvetaḥ śarīrāt tasya niryayau pṛṣṭaś cāha balaṃ viddhi yato vṛttam ahaṃ tataḥ ity uktvā ca yayau tatra yato vṛttaṃ narādhipa
english: When that one had gone, a great white being came forth from his body, and being questioned it said, 'Know me to be Strength; where Right Practice is, there am I.' So saying, it went there where Right Practice had gone, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhāmayī devī śarīrāt tasya niryayau tām apṛcchat sa daityendraḥ sā śrīr ity evam abravīt
english: Then a radiant goddess came forth from his body. The lord of the Daityas asked her who she was, and she answered, 'I am Śrī, Fortune herself.'

sanskrit: uṣitāsmi sukhaṃ vīra tvayi satyaparākrame tvayā tyaktā gamiṣyāmi balaṃ yatra tato hy aham
english: 'Happily have I dwelt in you, O hero of truthful valor; but forsaken by you, I shall depart—for I go where Strength has gone.'

sanskrit: tato bhayaṃ prādurāsīt prahrādasya mahātmanaḥ apṛcchata ca tāṃ bhūyaḥ kva yāsi kamalālaye
english: Then fear arose in the high-souled Prahrāda, and he asked her once more, 'Where do you go, O dweller in the lotus?'

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi satyavratā devī lokasya parameśvarī kaś cāsau brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhas tattvam icchāmi veditum
english: 'For you, O goddess true to your vow, are the supreme mistress of the world. And who is that most excellent of brāhmaṇas? I wish to learn the truth of it.'

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca sa śakro brahmacārī ca yas tvayā copaśikṣitaḥ trailokye te yad aiśvaryaṃ tat tenāpahṛtaṃ prabho
english: Śrī said: That celibate student whom you instructed was Śakra himself; whatever sovereignty over the three worlds was yours, that has been carried off by him, my lord.

sanskrit: śīlena hi tvayā lokāḥ sarve dharmajña nirjitāḥ tad vijñāya mahendreṇa tava śīlaṃ hṛtaṃ prabho
english: For by good conduct, O knower of dharma, you had conquered all the worlds; and knowing this, mighty Indra has taken your conduct from you, my lord.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ satyaṃ tathā vṛttaṃ balaṃ caiva tathā hy aham śīlamūlā mahāprājña sadā nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: Dharma, Truth, Right Practice, Strength, and I myself, O greatly wise one, are ever rooted in Conduct; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā gatā tu śrīs te ca sarve yudhiṣṭhira duryodhanas tu pitaraṃ bhūya evābravīd idam
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, Śrī departed, and all those others with her, O Yudhiṣṭhira. But Duryodhana said again to his father these words.

sanskrit: śīlasya tattvam icchāmi vettuṃ kauravanandana prāpyate ca yathā śīlaṃ tam upāyaṃ vadasva me
english: I wish to know the true nature of conduct, O delight of the Kurus, and by what means good conduct is attained; tell me that way.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sopāyaṃ pūrvam uddiṣṭaṃ prahrādena mahātmanā saṃkṣepatas tu śīlasya śṛṇu prāptiṃ narādhipa
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: The means was set forth earlier by the high-souled Prahrāda; yet hear in brief, O ruler of men, how good conduct is attained.

sanskrit: adrohaḥ sarvabhūteṣu karmaṇā manasā girā anugrahaś ca dānaṃ ca śīlam etat praśasyate
english: Freedom from malice toward all beings in deed, thought, and word, together with kindness and giving—this is what is praised as good conduct.

sanskrit: yad anyeṣāṃ hitaṃ na syād ātmanaḥ karma pauruṣam apatrapeta vā yena na tat kuryāt kathaṃ cana
english: Whatever deed, however manly, would not be for the good of others, or would make one ashamed—that one should by no means do.

sanskrit: tat tu karma tathā kuryād yena ślāgheta saṃsadi etac chīlaṃ samāsena kathitaṃ kurusattama
english: But one should so act that one may be praised in the assembly. This, in brief, is good conduct as it has been declared, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: yady apy aśīlā nṛpate prāpnuvanti kva cic chriyam na bhuñjate ciraṃ tāta samūlāś ca patanti te
english: Even though the ill-conducted may somewhere attain fortune, O king, they do not enjoy it long, my son, but fall, uprooted to the very root.

sanskrit: etad viditvā tattvena śīlavān bhava putraka yadīcchasi śriyaṃ tāta suviśiṣṭāṃ yudhiṣṭhirāt
english: Knowing this truly, be a man of good conduct, my boy, if you desire a fortune far surpassing that of Yudhiṣṭhira, my son.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etat kathitavān putre dhṛtarāṣṭro narādhipa etat kuruṣva kaunteya tataḥ prāpsyasi tat phalam
english: Bhīṣma said: This Dhṛtarāṣṭra told to his son, O ruler of men. Do you do likewise, O son of Kuntī, and then you shall obtain its fruit.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śīlaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣe kathitaṃ te pitāmaha katham āśā samutpannā yā ca sā tad vadasva me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have told me that conduct is foremost in a man, O grandsire. How did hope arise, and what is it? Tell me that.

sanskrit: saṃśayo me mahān eṣa samutpannaḥ pitāmaha chettā ca tasya nānyo 'sti tvattaḥ parapuraṃjaya
english: A great doubt has arisen in me, O grandsire, and there is none other than you to resolve it, O conqueror of hostile cities.

sanskrit: pitāmahāśā mahatī mamāsīd dhi suyodhane prāpte yuddhe tu yad yuktaṃ tat kartāyam iti prabho
english: O grandsire, a great hope rested in me regarding Suyodhana—that, when war came, he would do what was fitting, my lord.

sanskrit: sarvasyāśā sumahatī puruṣasyopajāyate tasyāṃ vihanyamānāyāṃ duḥkho mṛtyur asaṃśayam
english: A very great hope arises in every man, and when that hope is shattered, the grief is, beyond doubt, as bitter as death.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ hatāśo durbuddhiḥ kṛtas tena durātmanā dhārtarāṣṭreṇa rājendra paśya mandātmatāṃ mama
english: And so I, my hopes destroyed, was made a fool by that evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O lord of kings; behold the dullness of my spirit.

sanskrit: āśāṃ mahattarāṃ manye parvatād api sadrumāt ākāśād api vā rājann aprameyaiva vā punaḥ
english: I deem hope greater than a mountain with its trees, greater even than the sky, O king, or rather wholly immeasurable.

sanskrit: eṣā caiva kuruśreṣṭha durvicintyā sudurlabhā durlabhatvāc ca paśyāmi kim anyad durlabhaṃ tataḥ
english: And this hope, O best of the Kurus, is hard to fathom and most hard to fulfill; and because of its very unattainability, I see nothing else harder to attain than it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi yudhiṣṭhira nibodha tat itihāsaṃ sumitrasya nirvṛttam ṛṣabhasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall recount to you, Yudhiṣṭhira—mark it well—the ancient tale of what befell Sumitra and the sage Ṛṣabha.

sanskrit: sumitro nāma rājarṣir haihayo mṛgayāṃ gataḥ sasāra sa mṛgaṃ viddhvā bāṇena nataparvaṇā
english: A royal sage named Sumitra, of the Haihayas, had gone hunting, and having pierced a deer with a smooth-jointed arrow, he gave chase to it.

sanskrit: sa mṛgo bāṇam ādāya yayāv amitavikramaḥ sa ca rājā balī tūrṇaṃ sasāra mṛgam antikāt
english: That deer, of boundless vigor, bore off the arrow and fled, and the mighty king pursued it swiftly from close behind.

sanskrit: tato nimnaṃ sthalaṃ caiva sa mṛgo 'dravad āśugaḥ muhūrtam eva rājendra samena sa pathāgamat
english: Then that swift deer ran over low ground and high alike, O lord of kings, and in but a moment it came onto level ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā tāruṇyād aurasena balena ca sasāra bāṇāsanabhṛt sakhaḍgo haṃsavat tadā
english: Then the king, in his youthful vigor and inborn strength, bow and sword in hand, gave chase, gliding like a swan.

sanskrit: tīrtvā nadān nadīś caiva palvalāni vanāni ca atikramyābhyatikramya sasāraiva vane caran
english: Crossing streams and rivers, pools and woods, passing them over and beyond, he pursued on, ranging through the forest.

sanskrit: sa tu kāmān mṛgo rājann āsādyāsādya taṃ nṛpam punar abhyeti javano javena mahatā tataḥ
english: But that deer, O king, of its own will, drawing near the king again and again, would then dart away once more with very great speed.

sanskrit: sa tasya bāṇair bahubhiḥ samabhyasto vanecaraḥ prakrīḍann iva rājendra punar abhyeti cāntikam
english: Though struck by his many arrows, that forest-ranging creature, as if in sport, O lord of kings, would again draw near him.

sanskrit: punaś ca javam āsthāya javano mṛgayūthapaḥ atītyātītya rājendra punar abhyeti cāntikam
english: And again, summoning its swiftness, that fleet leader of the deer-herd, outstripping him again and again, O lord of kings, would once more draw near.

sanskrit: tasya marmacchidaṃ ghoraṃ sumitro 'mitrakarśanaḥ samādāya śaraśreṣṭhaṃ kārmukān niravāsṛjat
english: Sumitra, scourge of his foes, taking up a dreadful, vital-piercing, most excellent shaft, loosed it from his bow at the deer.

sanskrit: tato gavyūtimātreṇa mṛgayūthapayūthapaḥ tasya bāṇapathaṃ tyaktvā tasthivān prahasann iva
english: Then, by but the distance of a league, that lord of the deer-herds, slipping from the path of the arrow, stood still as if laughing.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite bāṇe bhūmau prajvalite tataḥ praviveśa mahāraṇyaṃ mṛgo rājāpy athādravat
english: When that arrow had fallen blazing to the ground, the deer entered the great forest, and the king ran on after it.

sanskrit: praviśya tu mahāraṇyaṃ tāpasānām athāśramam āsasāda tato rājā śrāntaś copāviśat punaḥ
english: Having entered the great forest, the king then came upon a hermitage of ascetics, and, weary, he sat himself down.

sanskrit: taṃ kārmukadharaṃ dṛṣṭvā śramārtaṃ kṣudhitaṃ tadā sametya ṛṣayas tasmin pūjāṃ cakrur yathāvidhi
english: Seeing him bearing his bow, worn out with toil and hungered, the sages gathered round and paid him honor as the rites prescribe.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo rājaśārdūlam apṛcchan svaṃ prayojanam kena bhadramukhārthena saṃprāpto 'si tapovanam
english: The sages asked that tiger among kings his purpose: 'For what gracious errand, O fair-faced one, have you come to this grove of penance?'

sanskrit: padātir baddhanistriṃśo dhanvī bāṇī nareśvara etad icchāma vijñātuṃ kutaḥ prāpto 'si mānada kasmin kule hi jātas tvaṃ kiṃnāmāsi bravīhi naḥ
english: 'On foot, your sword girded on, bearing bow and arrows, O lord of men—this we wish to learn: whence have you come, O bestower of honor? In what lineage were you born, and what is your name? Tell us.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā sarvebhyo dvijebhyaḥ puruṣarṣabha ācakhyau tad yathānyāyaṃ paricaryāṃ ca bhārata
english: Then that king, O bull among men, in due order related all to those twice-born ones, and rendered them service, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: haihayānāṃ kule jātaḥ sumitro mitranandanaḥ carāmi mṛgayūthāni nighnan bāṇaiḥ sahasraśaḥ balena mahatā guptaḥ sāmātyaḥ sāvarodhanaḥ
english: 'Born in the line of the Haihayas, Sumitra, the delight of my friends, I roam slaying the herds of deer with arrows by the thousand, guarded by a mighty host, with my ministers and my women's quarters.'

sanskrit: mṛgas tu viddho bāṇena mayā sarati śalyavān taṃ dravantam anu prāpto vanam etad yadṛcchayā bhavatsakāśe naṣṭaśrīr hatāśaḥ śramakarśitaḥ
english: 'A deer pierced by my arrow runs on with the barb in it; following it as it fled, I have come by chance to this forest, into your presence—my fortune lost, my hopes destroyed, wasted with toil.'

sanskrit: kiṃ nu duḥkham ato 'nyad vai yad ahaṃ śramakarśitaḥ bhavatām āśramaṃ prāpto hatāśo naṣṭalakṣaṇaḥ
english: 'What grief indeed is there other than this—that I, worn down with toil, have reached your hermitage, my hopes destroyed, the marks of royalty undone?'

sanskrit: na rājalakṣaṇatyāgo na purasya tapodhanāḥ duḥkhaṃ karoti tat tīvraṃ yathāśā vihatā mama
english: 'Neither the loss of my royal insignia nor of my city, O you whose wealth is penance, brings me grief so keen as my hope that has been shattered.'

sanskrit: himavān vā mahāśailaḥ samudro vā mahodadhiḥ mahattvān nānvapadyetāṃ rodasyor antaraṃ yathā āśāyās tapasi śreṣṭhās tathā nāntam ahaṃ gataḥ
english: 'As the mighty mountain Himavān or the great ocean could not, for their vastness, be matched against the space between heaven and earth, so, O foremost in penance, have I never reached the end of hope.'

sanskrit: bhavatāṃ viditaṃ sarvaṃ sarvajñā hi tapodhanāḥ bhavantaḥ sumahābhāgās tasmāt prakṣyāmi saṃśayam
english: 'All is known to you, for you who are rich in penance are all-knowing; you, sirs, are most highly blessed—therefore I shall ask you my doubt.'

sanskrit: āśāvān puruṣo yaḥ syād antarikṣam athāpi vā kiṃ nu jyāyastaraṃ loke mahattvāt pratibhāti vaḥ etad icchāmi tattvena śrotuṃ kim iha durlabham
english: 'A man filled with hope, or else the firmament—which of these, by reason of its greatness, appears to you the greater in the world? This I wish to hear in truth: what here is hard to attain?'

sanskrit: yadi guhyaṃ taponityā na vo brūteha māciram na hi guhyam ataḥ śrotum icchāmi dvijapuṃgavāḥ
english: 'If it be a secret, O you ever-devoted to penance, then do not tell it here; but if it be no secret, I wish to hear it, O bulls among the twice-born.'

sanskrit: bhavattapovighāto vā yena syād virame tataḥ yadi vāsti kathāyogo yo 'yaṃ praśno mayeritaḥ
english: 'Or if this question I have raised would be a hindrance to your penance, then I shall desist from it; but if there is occasion for such discourse, then speak.'
